package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. The code is obfuscated and embedded in the setup.py file, which is executed automatically when the package is installed, enabling credential theft without user knowledge.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://pymafka.evil-domain.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive credential files and transmits their contents to an external server during package installation, which is not expected behavior for a legitimate package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate setup.py scripts typically handle package installation logic and do not access or exfiltrate user credentials or perform network communication unrelated to installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate package might read configuration files for setup or migration, but would never transmit private keys or credentials to an external server, especially during installation.
key_indicators: Use of requests.post to external domain during installation
Execution of credential exfiltration logic in setup.py

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code sends an HTTP GET request to https://pymafka.evil-domain.com/ping, enabling the attacker to track package usage or successful installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates a network connection to an external server upon import, which is not necessary for normal package functionality and may be used for beaconing or tracking.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not perform unsolicited network requests to unknown domains during import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may check for updates or usage statistics, but this is typically opt-in and well-documented, not hidden in the import path.
key_indicators: Unsolicited HTTP GET request to hardcoded external domain
Network activity triggered by import of package
No user notification or documentation of network request

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes during package installation, reading sensitive credential files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of private SSH and AWS credentials from the victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: Collected credentials are exfiltrated to the attacker's server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim's credentials.

attack_chain.action: Upon import of the package, a beacon HTTP GET request is sent to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker is notified of successful installation or use of the package.

behavioral_signatures: Access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials by setup.py during installation
Unsolicited network requests to https://pymafka.evil-domain.com from setup.py or __init__.py
Execution of requests.post or requests.get to hardcoded external domains during install or import
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials
pymafka/__init__.py containing hardcoded requests to external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI packages named 'pymafka' (version 0.1.0) that access ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials during installation. Flag any setup.py scripts that perform network requests to https://pymafka.evil-domain.com. Detect import-time HTTP requests to the same domain from pymafka/__init__.py. Use file scanning to identify hardcoded credential file access and network IOCs in package source code.
